newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity nearby contracts settle higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity nearby contracts settle higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures for nearby months settled higher amid short-covering and stronger natural gas prices, but forward contracts were marginally lower, trade sources said Thursday.
"Everybody has been short for so long that every time the price goes down, they try to get out," said one dealer.
But the outer months were hit hard as players moved to flatten the price curve, especially for Palo Verde, she added.
Traders expected natural gas to continue giving near-term direction to power futures, with a breakout above $2.00 per million British thermal units seen as key.
On Thursday, the April Henry Hub gas contract on NYMEX settled at $1.839.
Still, little remains of winter weather, and "we are no where near air conditioning season," so demand is unlikely to pick up speed for a while, said another trader.
"There is still some room to move lower, but we should start seeing back-month PV and COB (California-Oregon border) start to move up," he noted.
Northwest temperatures were expected to average flat to four degrees F above normal for the next several days, but to fall below normal next week in most areas.
Over the same period, the Southwest was forecast to see much above normal temperatures in south and central sections, and above normal elsewhere.
The April COB contract settled 25 cents higher at $9.90 per megawatt hour (MWh), May was up 15 cents at $9.90 and June was up 15 cents at $10.45.
Other active COB contracts were between 35 cents higher and 10 cents lower.
April Palo Verde (PV) was up 15 cents at $13.95, while May was up 35 cents at $14.10 and June was up 5 cents at $15.50.
Other active PV contracts were 5 to 10 cents lower.
